chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majluwayh narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Husayn ibn Musa al-Khashab from Ghiyath ibn Kalub from Ishaq ibn Ammar from al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Impart to your dead the declaration 'La ilaha illa Allah' (There is no god but Allah), for whoever's last words are 'La ilaha illa Allah' will enter Paradise.

key_terms.لَقِّنُوا: Impart or teach gently, specifically referring to reciting the Shahadah to the dying.
key_terms.مَوْتَاکُمْ: Your dead (plural), referring to those who have passed away.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Talqeen and the Shahadah at the time of death in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* establishes the Sunnah of *Talqeen*, where the dying are reminded of the Shahadah to secure their final state of faith. It underscores the Shia belief in the efficacy of one's last utterance as a decisive criterion for Paradise, linking the physical act of recitation to the spiritual reality of *Tawhid*. This practice is rooted in the Prophet's instruction to ensure the dying person's heart remains firm on monotheism at the moment of death.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Ali Majluwayh from Muhammad b. Yahya from Muhammad b. Ahmad from al-Hussain b. Musa al-Khashab from Ghiyath b. Kalub from Ishaq b. Ammar from al-Sadiq Ja’far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (a.s.) that The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.s.) who said:
“Do Talqeen of ‘there is no god except Allah’, for a person whose last words are, ‘there is no god except Allah’, will enter Paradise.”
